prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
Travel in Japan may be changing in an unexpected way.

Young people, especially young men, are showing stronger interest in trips they can shape themselves. They want to travel alone, spend time on their hobbies, and leave room in the schedule. But the evidence does not show that they are already taking much longer trips.

A 2025 survey found that, among men aged 29 and under, solo travel was chosen by about 25%, while hobby-focused travel showed a similar level of interest. Another survey looked at Japanese Gen Z travelers with overseas experience. About 90% wanted free time inside a tour. Among them, about 80% wanted half a day or more.

These answers point to a wish for more control over the schedule. Yet the stays reported in travel plans remain short. In a 2024 autumn survey of people planning trips, the average stay was about 1.8 nights, with a median of 2 nights.

There is another interesting contrast. When people were asked to imagine taking a one-month holiday, the most common answer was a trip of about one week. That answer was chosen by about 24% of people.

So this is not a simple story of young people moving from sightseeing to long stays. The wish for a slower, more personal trip may be growing before the number of nights changes. A 2025 Tourism Agency white paper says Japan needs to increase the number of trips per person and make stays longer. For now, longer stays remain a goal, not a settled pattern.

【Point One】
A two-night trip can still feel different if the traveler chooses the pace. Even inside a package tour, a free half-day or a hobby-based option can give people more control. For tourism businesses, a practical response may be to leave parts of short trips open, rather than treat a longer holiday as the only form of slow travel.

【Point Two】
The young-traveler story is not one shared switch from sightseeing to slow travel. Among people aged 29 and under, young men favor solo and hobby-focused trips, while young women show about 52% interest in food travel and about 45% interest in famous sights. Solo travel is also the leading format among men aged 18 to 29. Planners should offer several kinds of products, not one answer for a whole generation.

point_one.reasoning: 短期旅行でも自由時間や趣味の選択によって旅行体験の質を変えられるという解釈を示し、旅行業者には日数を延ばす以外に旅程を部分的に開放するという具体策を提示している。Full Storyの調査結果を繰り返すだけでなく、「短期でもスローな旅行になり得る」という実務的な含意を加えている。

point_two.reasoning: 若年層を一括りにせず、若い男性の一人旅・趣味旅行と、若い女性の食・名所旅行への関心を対比し、商品設計を分ける必要性を示している。Full Storyにはなかった性別別の具体的データと、それに基づくターゲット設計の示唆があり、新しい価値を加えている。
